newsitem.title: USA: Acquisitive Humana to buy ChoiceCare for $250 million.
newsitem.headline: Acquisitive Humana to buy ChoiceCare for $250 million.

text.p: Managed health care company Humana Inc. said Thursday it agreed to buy ChoiceCare Corp., an HMO in Cincinnati, for $250 million in cash.
In a move that met with mixed reactions on Wall Street, Humana said it signed a definitive agreement to buy all outstanding ChoiceCare common shares for $16.38 each.
News of the deal followed by just two days Humana's announcement that it agreed to purchase Physician Corp. of America, a Miami, Fla.-based HMO, in a deal worth about $400 million.
The two deals combined would make Louisville, Ky.-based Humana the third-largest U.S. HMO company in enrollment and revnues, the company said.
The ChoiceCare acquisition will make Humana the largest health maintenance organisation in the solid Cincinnati market, but it may also distract management, analysts said.

"The broader issue is that Humana has things in its old business that it needs to fix and that's not going to be the only focus anymore because now they have to integrate these two companies," said Ed Kroll, a managed healthcare industry analyst at Furman Selz, a New York investment bank.
The two acquisitions will boost Humana's membership to 6.2 million from 4.8 million, and increase its premiums to $8.5 billion annually from $6.8 billion.
The acquisitions also may strengthen Humana's position in the key Florida and MidSouth markets, analysts said.
"If they integrate them well, these acquisitions will make Humana stronger in those regions," said Kenneth Abramowitz, an industry analyst at the Sanford Bernstein investment bank.

In a statement, Humana said it had obtained a $1.5 billion revolving credit facility from Chase Manhattan Bank to help finance the two deals. Humana said it expected to close the ChoiceCare acquisition this fall.
ChoiceCare serves more than 245,000 members. The ChoiceCare Foundation owns 91 percent of its 14.8 million shares; physicians and other employees own the rest, according to a ChoiceCare spokesman.
